items.title: Effect of Screening with Multicancer Early-Detection Test on Late-Stage Cancer Diagnosis.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether screening with blood-based early-detection tests for multiple cancers in addition to usual care has clinical utility is unknown.
METHODS: In a randomized, controlled trial conducted in England, we obtained peripheral blood from persons 50 to 77 years of age at up to three annual visits. After baseline blood collection, participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention group (participants whose blood was tested) or the control group (participants whose blood was stored). Participants and trial personnel were initially unaware of the group assignments. The primary end point was stage III or IV cancer among 12 prespecified types of cancer, and a key secondary end point was stage IV cancer among the 12 prespecified types. The differences between the groups in the incidence rate (the number of first eligible events divided by person-years at risk) were measured after three screening rounds and at least 12 months of follow-up after the last participant's third visit.
RESULTS: Overall, 71,122 participants were randomly assigned to the intervention group and 71,128 to the control group. The incidence rate of stage III or IV cancer (primary end point) did not differ significantly between the groups (incidence rate ratio [intervention vs. control], 1.03; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.92 to 1.14, P = 0.63). The incidence rate ratio for stage IV cancer (a key secondary end point) after 3 screening rounds was 0.86 (95% CI, 0.74 to 1.00). Less than 1% of participants had trial-related adverse events; none were serious.
CONCLUSIONS: In this trial, we did not observe a lower incidence rate of stage III or IV cancers across 12 prespecified cancers after three screening rounds with multicancer early-detection testing plus usual care than with usual care alone. Further follow-up is warranted to assess the way in which findings for stage III or IV cancers and the between-group difference in stage IV cancers evolve over time. (Funded by Grail; NHS-Galleri ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05611632; ISRCTN number, ISRCTN91431511.).

items.title: Tricuspid-Valve Intervention in Heart Failure.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effect of transcatheter tricuspid-valve repair on clinical outcomes, including death and hospitalization for heart failure, in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation remains uncertain.
METHODS: We randomly assigned patients with symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation and an increased risk of future heart-failure events in a 2:1 ratio to tricuspid-valve repair plus medical therapy (tricuspid-repair group) or medical therapy alone (medical-therapy group). The first primary end point was a hierarchical composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, and quality-of-life improvement at 1 year, assessed by win ratio. If the between-group difference was significant, a second primary end point would be tested: a composite of death from any cause or hospitalization for heart failure through 3 years.
RESULTS: A total of 360 patients underwent randomization (237 patients were assigned to the tricuspid-repair group and 123 to the medical-therapy group). The mean (±SD) age of the patients was 80.3±6.4 years, and 56.4% were women. The win ratio for the first primary end point was 2.42 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.76 to 3.33; P<0.001), favoring tricuspid-valve repair. The Kaplan-Meier estimate for freedom from death from any cause or hospitalization for heart failure (second primary end point) through 3 years was 52.4% (95% CI, 43.2 to 63.6) in the tricuspid-repair group and 21.0% (95% CI, 12.7 to 34.6) in the medical-therapy group (hazard ratio for death from any cause or hospitalization for heart failure, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.29 to 0.55; P<0.001). Major adverse events within 30 days occurred in 14 patients (5.9%) in the tricuspid-repair group.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation, transcatheter tricuspid-valve repair plus medical therapy was superior to medical therapy alone with respect to a hierarchical composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, and quality-of-life improvement at 1 year and was also associated with a lower risk of a composite of death from any cause or hospitalization for heart failure through 3 years. (Funded by the German Center for Cardiovascular Research and others; TRIC-I-HF ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04634266.).

items.title: Disitamab Vedotin Plus Tislelizumab in Transurethrally Unresectable, ERBB2-Positive, Non-Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: A Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Very high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (VHR NMIBC) includes extensive high-grade T1 (T1HG) disease, T1HG with carcinoma in situ, variant histology, lymphovascular invasion, or bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG)-unresponsive disease. Transurethrally unresectable disease warrants radical cystectomy, but patients ineligible for or declining cystectomy lack established nonsurgical therapy.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of disitamab vedotin (DV, an anti-ERBB2 [formerly HER2] antibody-drug conjugate) plus tislelizumab (an anti-programmed cell death 1 protein immune checkpoint inhibitor) in transurethrally unresectable ERBB2-positive VHR NMIBC.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was an open-label, single-arm, phase 2, nonrandomized clinical trial with a Simon 2-stage design, conducted in an academic hospital from August 2022 to May 2024 with a median follow-up of 29.4 months. The analysis included adults with transurethrally unresectable ERBB2-positive NMIBC who met the 2019 European Association of Urology VHR criteria and who were ineligible for or declined cystectomy.
INTERVENTION: Patients received an intravenous injection of DV (120 mg, day 1) plus tislelizumab (200 mg, day 2) every 3 weeks for 3 cycles; patients who responded received up to 8 DV cycles and 17 tislelizumab cycles.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was complete response (CR) of high-risk disease, defined as no high-grade tumor, T1 disease, carcinoma in situ, or progression. Secondary outcomes were response duration, progression-free survival, overall survival, and safety.
RESULTS: Among 137 screened patients, 28 participants (median [IQR] age, 72 [67-74] years; 25 male [89%]) were included. Two preassessment withdrawals were counted as nonresponders in the all-treated analysis, which left 26 efficacy-evaluable patients. CR of high-risk disease was achieved in 19 of 26 (73.1%; 95% CI, 54.8%-91.3%), meeting the prespecified 70% alternative-rate goal. Among all 28, 19 responded (67.9%; 95% CI, 49.4%-86.3%), exceeding the 17-response exact binomial threshold. Both analyses met the primary criterion. Among responders, the 24-month sustained response was 83.5% (95% CI, 68.0%-100.0%), and no muscle invasive or metastatic progression occurred. Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 25 patients (89.3%), most commonly paresthesia (12 [42.9%]), alopecia (11 [39.3%]), and pruritus (10 [35.7%]); 4 (14.3%) had grade 3 to 4 events; 2 (7.1%) discontinued treatment; and none had grade 5 events.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Findings of this nonrandomized clinical trial suggest that DV plus tislelizumab may show a high CR rate and durable disease control in patients with transurethrally unresectable ERBB2-positive VHR NMIBC, supporting randomized clinical trials.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05495724.

items.title: Nicotinamide Riboside for Patients With Early-Stage Parkinson Disease: The NOPARK Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Nicotinamide riboside, a nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide precursor, has been proposed as a potential disease-modifying therapy for Parkinson disease based on preclinical and early studies. Whether prolonged oral nicotinamide riboside improves clinical outcomes in Parkinson disease is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether nicotinamide riboside improves clinical outcomes in Parkinson disease compared with placebo.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 clinical trial conducted at 11 centers in Norway. Eligible participants were patients aged 35 years or older with Parkinson disease diagnosed within 2 years before enrollment, Hoehn and Yahr disease stage less than 3, abnormal dopamine transporter scintigraphy findings confirming dopaminergic nigrostriatal denervation, and stable dopaminergic treatment before enrollment. Of 537 screened individuals, 410 were randomized from May 6, 2020, to June 20, 2024, and 393 were included in the primary analysis. Final follow-up was completed on June 19, 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to receive oral nicotinamide riboside, 500 mg twice daily (n = 206), or matching placebo (n = 204) for 52 weeks.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was change from baseline to week 52 in the Movement Disorder Society Unified Parkinson Disease Rating Scale total score (MDS-UPDRS parts I-III; range, 0-236, with higher scores indicating more severe disease; clinically important differences for improvement and worsening, 6.7 and 5.2 points, respectively), analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures. The 5 key secondary outcomes were the individual parts I, II, and III of the MDS-UPDRS; dopamine transporter single-photon emission computed tomography brain imaging findings; and the Non-Motor Symptoms Scale score (NMSS; range, 0-360, with higher scores indicating greater nonmotor symptom burden).
RESULTS: Among the 393 participants in the primary analysis, the mean age was 65.6 (SD, 9.4) years and 133 (34%) were female. At week 52, the total MDS-UPDRS score increased by 2.45 (95% CI, 0.80-4.10) points with nicotinamide riboside and decreased by 0.27 (95% CI, -1.95 to 1.40) points with placebo, yielding an adjusted mean difference of 2.72 points (95% CI, 0.47-4.98 points; P = .02), favoring placebo. Of the 5 prespecified key secondary outcomes, 4 showed no significant difference, but nonmotor symptom burden worsened more with nicotinamide riboside (NMSS score adjusted mean difference, 4.22 [95% CI, 1.07-7.37] points; P = .009). Serious adverse events occurred in 17 (8.3%) of 205 participants receiving nicotinamide riboside and 29 (14.1%) of 205 receiving placebo in the safety population.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among patients with early Parkinson disease, nicotinamide riboside treatment for 52 weeks did not improve clinical outcomes and was associated with worse clinical outcomes than placebo. These findings do not support nicotinamide riboside as a disease-modifying treatment for Parkinson disease.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03568968.

items.title: Vasopressors or Fluids in Early Septic Shock.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
authors: ARISE FLUIDS Investigators, the ANZICS Clinical Trials Group, and the ACEM Clinical Trials Network
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal approach to early resuscitation in septic shock is unknown. Equipoise exists between the use of larger volumes of intravenous fluids to restore perfusion and the use of early vasopressor therapy along with smaller volumes of fluids to minimize potential harm from excess fluid.
METHODS: We randomly assigned adult patients who presented to the emergency department with septic shock to receive either fluids at restricted volumes and early vasopressor therapy (vasopressor group) or higher volumes of fluids and later vasopressor therapy (fluids group) for at least 6 hours and up to 24 hours. The primary outcome was days alive and out of the hospital from randomization to day 90.
RESULTS: A total of 1000 patients underwent randomization, with 499 assigned to the vasopressor group and 501 to the fluids group. Informed consent was not obtained for 37 patients, which left 963 patients in the intention-to-treat population (481 in the vasopressor group and 482 in the fluids group). Three patients in the fluids group were lost to follow-up for the primary outcome. In the first 24 hours after randomization, patients in the vasopressor group received less intravenous fluid than those in the fluids group (median difference, -1108 ml; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1395 to -850). The percentage of patients who received vasopressors was higher by 18.9 percentage points (95% CI, 13.3 to 24.5) in the vasopressor group. The median number of days alive and out of the hospital at day 90 was 76 (interquartile range, 55 to 83) in the vasopressor group and 76 (interquartile range, 55 to 82) in the fluids group (difference, 0.0 days; 95% CI, -2.7 to 2.7; P = 1.00). Adverse events occurred in similar percentages of patients in the two groups, except for pulmonary edema (0.6% in the vasopressor group vs. 5.0% in the fluids group; P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Among adult patients who presented to the emergency department with septic shock, an approach that involved restricted fluid volume and early vasopressors did not result in a greater number of days alive and out of the hospital at day 90 than an approach involving greater fluid volume and later administration of vasopressors. items.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Phenobarbital vs Diazepam for Alcohol Withdrawal Syndrome.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Phenobarbital use for alcohol withdrawal syndrome is increasing, but its effectiveness and safety have largely been compared with lorazepam rather than against more pharmacokinetically similar long-acting, self-tapering benzodiazepines such as diazepam.
OBJECTIVE: To emulate a clinical trial comparing patients randomized to phenobarbital vs diazepam for alcohol withdrawal syndrome.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter comparative effectiveness research study analyzed data from the Premier Healthcare Database (October 2022 to August 2024), representing 754 US acute care hospitals. Adult inpatients with a primary diagnosis of alcohol withdrawal syndrome present on admission who initiated phenobarbital or diazepam on the day of hospital admission were included.
EXPOSURES: Initiation of phenobarbital or diazepam on the day of hospital admission.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary effectiveness outcome was hospital length of stay in days. The primary safety outcome was invasive mechanical ventilation use. Secondary outcomes assessed treatment escalation, complications of severe alcohol withdrawal syndrome, and resource utilization. Targeted maximum likelihood estimation with ensemble machine learning was used to estimate marginal mean differences and risk differences between exposure groups.
RESULTS: Among 24 643 patients (median [IQR] age, 45 [35-56] years; 18 511 male [75.1%]), 11 919 (48.4%) received phenobarbital and 12 724 (51.6%) received diazepam on the day of admission. There were no differences in hospital length of stay (marginal mean, 4.1 vs 4.3 days; marginal mean difference, -0.21 [95% CI, -0.42 to 0.00] days) or invasive mechanical ventilation use (marginal risk, 3.1% vs 2.7%; marginal risk difference, 0.4% [95% CI, -0.7% to 1.4%]) between initiation of phenobarbital vs diazepam. Secondary outcomes were also not different between phenobarbital and diazepam, except for self-directed discharge, which was more frequent among those initiated on diazepam (marginal risk, 9.5% vs 12.6%; marginal risk difference, -3.1% [95% CI, -4.9% to -1.3%]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this multicenter study of patients hospitalized for alcohol withdrawal syndrome, there were no differences in hospital length of stay or the need for invasive mechanical ventilation between initiation of phenobarbital vs diazepam. These results may suggest near therapeutic equivalence between phenobarbital and long-acting benzodiazepines.

items.title: Communicating Uncertainties About the Benefits and Risks of New Cancer Drugs: Two Randomized Clinical Trials.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cancer drugs are frequently approved based on uncertain benefits and risks that are not communicated to patients.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of communicating uncertainties about the benefits and risks of new cancer drugs on changes in individuals' hypothetical decisions to take the drug.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Two randomized clinical trials recruited online a demographically diverse sample of US adults (census matched for age, sex, education, income, and race and ethnicity) from May 9 to July 26, 2025.
INTERVENTION: Plain-language statements describing uncertainties about drug benefits and risks. Trial 1 randomized participants to 1 of 5 uncertainties: (1) single-arm trial design, (2) unrepresentative population in terms of race and ethnicity, (3) short study duration, (4) surrogate end point, or (5) no noticeable improvement. Trial 2 randomized participants to 1, 2, 3, or 4 uncertainties or to a control group.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome in trial 1 was changes in hypothetical decisions to take a new cancer drug (within-group difference), while in trial 2 the primary outcome was the change in between-group differences in hypothetical decisions (control vs intervention groups). Secondary outcomes included perceived treatment effectiveness, worry associated with taking the drug, and trust in the information and the US Food and Drug Administration.
RESULTS: A total of 6272 adults were included in the primary analysis (3102 [49.5%] women). In trial 1, learning about uncertainties reduced hypothetical decisions to take the drug by a mean of 10.1 percentage points (pp; 95% CI, -11.7 to -8.5 pp; P < .001). The reduction in hypothetical decisions to take the drug was observed for all uncertainties, including among those in the group that learned that it was unknown whether patients would notice an improvement with the drug (-14.1 pp; 95% CI, -17.9 to -10.4 pp; P < .001) and those who learned that the drug was not studied in patients of similar race or ethnicity (-12.8 pp; 95% CI, -16.4 to -9.2; P < .001). In trial 2, hypothetical decisions to take the drug decreased with each additional uncertainty, demonstrating a dose-dependent effect. Learning about uncertainties reduced perceived effectiveness and trust but did not affect worry.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In 2 randomized clinical trials including a demographically diverse sample of US adults, learning about common uncertainties with a new cancer drug's benefits and risks reduced hypothetical decisions to take the drug.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifiers: NCT06997185 and NCT07110597.

items.title: The conformation-selective PI3Kδ inhibitor roginolisib in patients with advanced or metastatic cancer, including metastatic uveal melanoma: first-in-human clinical trial.
items.abstract: Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase delta (PI3Kδ) promotes tumour cell growth directly or indirectly by activating immune-suppressive cells. In contrast to previous PI3Kδ inhibitors, roginolisib is a selective, non-ATP competitive inhibitor, which locks PI3Kδ into an inactive state and causes an allosteric modulation. In a First-in-Human dose study, continuous daily dosing of roginolisib was investigated in patients with solid and haematologic malignancies. In Part A, 24 patients received escalating doses of roginolisib. In Part B, 20 mostly pre-treated metastatic uveal melanoma (mUM) patients received a dose associated with continuous PI3Kδ inhibition of >90%. The primary endpoint was safety, and secondary endpoints included pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) profile, clinical anti-tumour responses assessments. Exploratory endpoints included immunophenotyping, proteomics, genomics. No Dose Limiting Toxicity or drug related toxicities requiring dose modifications were observed ( ≥ Grade 3 toxicities: 3/44; 6.8%). In mUM, median Overall Survival (mOS) was 20.8 months (data-cut off December 2023) and 18.4 months (data-cut-off February 2026). mOS in mUM patients with Stable Disease at Week 16 ( = Cycle 5) was 28.5 months, while patients who progressed at Week 16 had a median OS of 12.3 months. Roginolisib was safe, had a predictable PK profile, T regulatory cell abundance was decreased while activated CD8+ T cells increased together with soluble plasma IL-15. ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT04328844.

items.title: Invasive interval breast cancer rates after digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised mammography versus digital mammography screening (TOSYMA): 24-month follow-up of the multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite high invasive breast cancer detection rates, the effectiveness of digital breast tomosynthesis screening is still uncertain. We aimed to compare the invasive interval cancer rates in women screened with digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised two-dimensional (s2D) mammography with those screened with digital mammography.
METHODS: TOSYMA is a multicentre, open-label, parallel-group, randomised, controlled, superiority trial done at 17 screening sites across two federal states in Germany. Women aged 50-70 years were randomly allocated (1:1) to digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography or digital mammography. The first primary endpoint of TOSYMA (TOSYMA-1) was the detection rate of invasive breast cancer and has been previously reported. The second primary endpoint (TOSYMA-2) was the invasive interval cancer rate, defined as the proportion of women who developed an invasive breast cancer in the 24-month interval after being negative at screening (ie, no ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive breast cancer detection) in TOSYMA-1. The primary endpoint was analysed in all participants with a negative screening result in TOSYMA-1. The cumulative incidence of invasive interval cancers at 12 months in screen-negative women was the prespecified secondary outcome. Suspected interval cancers were identified by data linkage to cancer registries. The study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03377036) and is closed to accrual but follow-up is ongoing.
FINDINGS: Between July 5, 2018, and Dec 30, 2020, 99 689 women were enrolled in TOSYMA-1 and 99 558 participants included in the modified full analysis set of TOSYMA-1. The median age was 57 years (IQR 53-62) in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set and all participants were female. 49 299 (99·1%) of 49 762 women assigned digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screened negative in TOSYMA-1, as were 49 456 (99·3%) of 49 796 women assigned digital mammography who had evaluable data and were included in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set. Invasive interval cancers were detected in 70 of 49 299 women in the digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography group (invasive interval rate 14·2 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result) and in 92 of 49 456 women in the digital mammography group (18·6 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result; adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0·76 [95% CI 0·55-1·06]; p=0·11). Invasive interval cancers were detected within 12 months in 22 women in the digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography group (4·5 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result) and in 31 women in the digital mammography group (6·3 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result; OR 0·71 [95% CI 0·52-0·97]).
INTERPRETATION: TOSYMA-2 indicates that about a quarter of invasive interval cancers occurring with digital mammography over 2 years might be avoided with digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screening. Although the primary outcome of TOSYMA-2 did not reach statistical significance, this large, randomised trial adds substantial evidence to the use of digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography in breast cancer screening.

items.title: Shared patterns of human milk composition link mammary gland function to infant growth.
items.abstract: The mammary gland produces nutrient-rich human milk (HM), yet how mammary functional state shapes HM composition and infant outcomes remains poorly understood. We used HM multi-omics - metabolomics, proteomics, micronutrients, macronutrients, and HM oligosaccharides - across 1,543 samples from three cohorts, including two randomized trials, as a noninvasive readout of mammary functional state. Trajectory modeling and multi-omic integration showed that maternal supplementation improved recovery from early growth faltering and revealed a shared HM compositional axis linking maternal nutrition to infant growth. Machine learning, with Human Protein Atlas-informed proteomics, identified seven HM biomarkers reflecting variation across key mammary domains, indexing milk synthesis, barrier integrity, and immune/repair activity. Elevated valerylcarnitine and low pantothenic acid emerged as metabolic signals linking mammary functional state to infant growth.

items.title: Plasma Phosphorylated Tau 217 Percentage by Race and Ethnicity in Preclinical Alzheimer Disease.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In trials targeting preclinical Alzheimer disease (AD), defined as amyloid pathology without cognitive symptoms, racial and ethnic differences in plasma phosphorylated tau 217 percentage (%p-tau217) may influence screening eligibility.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize racial and ethnic differences in %p-tau217 and determine whether associations between %p-tau217, cognition, and amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) differ across groups.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a cross-sectional analysis of AHEAD 3-45 screening participants conducted from July 2020 to October 2024 at 106 sites across 4 world regions. Adults aged 55 to 80 years with %p-tau217 measured before medical and cognitive exclusions (N = 15 612) were included.
EXPOSURES: Self-reported race (Asian, Black, and White) and ethnicity (Hispanic and non-Hispanic) and apolipoprotein E ε4 (APOE ε4) carrier status.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: %p-tau217 levels and associations of %p-tau217 with Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite 5 (PACC5) score and amyloid PET were evaluated across racial and ethnic groups using multivariable linear regression.
RESULTS: Among 15 612 participants, the mean (SD) age was 68.4 (6.2) years; 9941 (63.7%) were female and 5755 (36.9%) were APOE ε4 carriers. %p-tau217 levels were lower among Asian, Black, and Hispanic participants than among White and non-Hispanic participants. APOE ε4 status was associated with higher %p-tau217 across all groups. The association between APOE ε4 status and %p-tau217 differed by race (APOE ε4 × race: F2,14 973 = 10.06; P < .001) and ethnicity (APOE ε4 × ethnicity: β, 0.042; 95% CI, 0.017 to 0.067; P = .005) (Asian: β, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.02 to 0.08; P = .01; Black: β, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.03 to 0.08; P = .002; Hispanic: β, 0.04; 95% CI, 0.02 to 0.07; P = .005). The %p-tau217-PACC5 association showed no pairwise differences across racial groups but differed by ethnicity (β, -0.53; 95% CI, -0.85 to -0.21; P = .008) and APOE ε4 × ethnicity (β, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.26 to 1.30; P = .02). The %p-tau217-PET association showed no significant pairwise differences across racial groups but differed by ethnicity (β, -6.30; 95% CI, -9.10 to -3.51; P < .001) and APOE ε4 × ethnicity (β, 7.12; 95% CI, 2.52 to 11.73; P = .01).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cross-sectional study, plasma %p-tau217 varied across racial and ethnic groups. Consistent %p-tau217-PACC5 score and %p-tau217-PET associations across racial groups support plasma-based screening before PET confirmation, while ethnicity-related findings warrant further investigation.

items.title: Global Incidence of All-Cause Dementia: A Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Global dementia incidence estimates are limited by underrepresentation of low- and middle-income countries and heterogeneous analytic methods. Due to these limitations, true understanding of the global dementia landscape remains incomplete.
OBJECTIVE: To identify dementia incidence rates by age and sex in various regions worldwide (high-income countries and low- and middle-income countries) where data on clinically based dementia diagnoses were available.
DATA SOURCES: Retrospective community-based cohorts from the Cohort Studies of Memory in an International Consortium (COSMIC); baseline recruitment commenced between January 1990 and December 2011 and follow-up data were collected through the end of 2021. Data were analyzed from June 2024 to June 2025.
STUDY SELECTION: Eligible studies included longitudinal COSMIC cohort studies with a clinically based diagnosis of dementia. Individual participant-level data from 22 population-based longitudinal cohorts (N = 38 418) spanning 18 countries or territories across 6 continents were included.
DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Data extraction and assessment of study quality and validity were conducted according to Meta-Analyses of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (MOOSE) guidelines. Individual participant-level data were meta-analyzed in a 2-step process using random intercepts for country and study at the global and regional levels and by country income level.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: For each study with a clinically based diagnosis, incidence rates for all-cause dementia were calculated and a 2-step meta-analysis was conducted. Using a person-years at risk framework with inverse-probability censoring weights and Poisson models, age- and sex-specific incidence were estimated and then standardized to the 2023 global age-sex population structure.
RESULTS: Across 287 632 person-years at risk, 3001 participants developed dementia. Age- and sex-standardized incidence was 9.7 (95% CI, 7.89-11.97) per 1000 person-years at risk. Age-standardized incidence was higher in women than men (10.6; 95% CI, 8.61-13.11 vs 8.6; 95% CI, 6.94-10.72). Standardized incidence was higher in low- and middle-income countries (13.6; 95% CI, 9.67-19.24) than in high-income countries (8.3; 95% CI, 6.57-10.54). Applying age- and sex-specific rates to the projected 2050 population yielded a projected 24.7 million new cases, assuming constant incidence over time.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The harmonized estimates presented in this study provide a comparable benchmark for global dementia incidence and inform planning for prevention, diagnosis, and memory-care services, particularly in underrepresented low- and middle-income country settings.

items.title: Targeting CD28 on T lineage malignancies with chimeric antigen receptor T cells.
items.abstract: Currently, no immunotherapy is approved for T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T‑ALL). High initial response rates to CD7‑directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells are limited by profound T cell aplasia and CD7‑negative immune escape, underscoring the need for alternative targets. Here, we show that CD28 is overexpressed on T‑ALL blasts from children and adolescents compared with lymphoid progenitors from healthy donors and is uniformly upregulated in nodal T-follicular helper cell lymphomas (nTFHL-AI, nTFHL-F). Using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated CD28 knockout to prevent fratricide, we generate highly functional anti‑CD28 CAR T cells with selective cytotoxicity against CD28⁺ T‑ALL. Anti‑CD28 CAR T cells match anti‑CD7 CAR T cells in vitro and in vivo, but cause markedly less lymphodepletion, largely sparing CD8 T cells and NK cells while preferentially depleting CD4 T cells, particularly TH2 and TH17 subsets. These findings establish CD28 as an actionable target for CAR T cell therapy of T cell malignancies.

items.title: Nutritional interventions' impacts on human milk: Three trials in low-resource settings.
items.abstract: Human milk (HM) composition is variable to support changing infant needs and is influenced by maternal diet and health. We harmonized HM data from three randomized trials in Burkina Faso (MISAME-III), Pakistan (Mumta-LW), and Tanzania (ELICIT) within the International Milk Composition (IMiC) Consortium to test how maternal nutrition affects HM composition. Balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplements or nicotinamide given to lactating mothers increased milk B-vitamins, while macronutrients, oligosaccharides, bioactive proteins, and microbiome composition were physiologically buffered. Metabolomic and proteomic analyses revealed shifts in vitamin-related metabolites, triglyceride profiles, and intracellular protein representation. In a MISAME-III subset, maternal and infant blood showed concordant changes. Postnatal BEP improved infant growth only in the more undernourished cohort. Improved milk micronutrient quality across settings supports extending maternal supplementation into lactation.
